title: Tate and anabelian Hom recover different kinds of morphism
quote: conj. de Hodge et de Tate; dans quelle mesure un morphisme de préschémas … est connu par le foncteur sur les motifs
context: Adds a reconstruction comparison to context/MPL_16+47+54+44_transcription.tex, cote16/021, L864, and cote16/049, L1829; differs from their Tate-sheaf definition and conditional algebraic-splitting programme; no anabelian Hom theorem was located in that supplied transcription
ledger: MPL_14_002-044 §3 [observation (research note of a returned package, first pass; a lead)]; MPL_14_087-132 §81 [observation (research note of a returned package, first pass; a lead)]
body: Tate (1966, main theorem) identifies \(\operatorname{Hom}_k(A,B)\otimes\mathbf Z_\ell\) with \(G_k\)-equivariant homomorphisms of Tate modules for abelian varieties over a finite field and \(\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k\). For hyperbolic curves over a sub-\(p\)-adic field, Mochizuki (1999, Theorem A) identifies dominant morphisms with continuous open homomorphisms of arithmetic fundamental groups over the fixed absolute Galois group, modulo geometric inner conjugacy. These give two precise reconstruction maps with different bases, objects and allowed morphisms; neither identifies the manuscript’s entire motivic essential image.

title: Semisimplicity does not imply a trivial centre
quote: Elle est triviale pour les motifs simples; \(G(X,\xi)=\underline{\operatorname{Aut}}(\xi)\)
context: Restates the conditional semisimplicity setting of context/MPL_16+47+54+44_transcription.tex, cote16/049, L1829, and context/MPL_16+47+54+44_notes.md, S13–S16; adds a counterexample to a centre-free inference, which those witnesses do not assert
ledger: MPL_14_087-132 M09 [Unpursued implication: semisimplicity a… (research note of a returned package, first pass; a lead)]; WG2 §2.3 #7 [question or plan item of the war game (round 2; unchecked)]
body: For a connected affine group scheme in characteristic zero, semisimplicity of its representation category is equivalent to pro-reductivity (Deligne & Milne, 1982/2012, Proposition 2.23). Yet \(\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathbf Q}(\mathbf G_m)\) decomposes into characters while \(Z(\mathbf G_m)=\mathbf G_m\). The geometric profinite group of a characteristic-zero hyperbolic curve is independently slim, enabling recovery of its arithmetic extension from the outer Galois action (Mochizuki, 2004, Lemma 1.3.1 and Corollary 1.3.2). Confidence: high, because the explicit character decomposition proves the counterexample; neither this calculation nor the profinite theorem establishes the manuscript’s conditional motivic semisimplicity.

title: Polarization and real-section reconstruction impose different conditions
quote: motifs polarisés rigidifiés; structure de Hodge; réellification
context: Adds a real-structure comparison to context/MPL_16+47+54+44_transcription.tex, cote44/002, L2803, and cote44/008–009, L2979–2989; differs from the positivity problem for the proposed canonical self-duality
ledger: MPL_14_002-044 A36 [Unpursued implication: the modern autod… (research note of a returned package, first pass; a lead)]; WG2 §2.3 #12 [question or plan item of the war game (round 2; unchecked)]
body: An algebraic Tannakian category over \(\mathbf R\) is polarizable exactly when its band is defined by a compact real algebraic group (Deligne & Milne, 1982/2012, Theorem 4.17(a)). For a smooth projective hyperbolic curve over \(\mathbf R\), the real-section theorem instead identifies connected components of the real locus with conjugacy classes of sections of its arithmetic fundamental-group sequence (Pál, 2011, Theorem 1.3). The first condition includes positivity, while the second recovers components; neither turns the manuscript’s two real involutions into a polarization or separates all individual real points and archimedean places.

title: Non-Tate weights give a precise cuspidal-inertia criterion
quote: ne provient pas d’une filtration du motif; filtration de Hodge -- non motivique --
context: Adds a nonlinear use of the Tate sheaf defined in context/MPL_16+47+54+44_transcription.tex, cote16/021, L864, and of the twist in cote44/008, L2974; differs from the manuscript’s Hodge-filtration and motivic-level discussion
ledger: MPL_14_002-044 B04 [Weights and cyclotomic normalizers (research note of a returned package, first pass; a lead)]; LM7 C.1 [Known (the return's claim)]; LM7 C.8 [Refuted (the return's claim)]
body: For a characteristic-zero hyperbolic curve over a field with non-Tate \(\ell\)-adic cyclotomic character, Stix (2012, Definition 29 and Theorem 30) characterizes cuspidal closed geometric \(\mathbf Z_\ell\)-subgroups by a normalizing subgroup with open Galois image and cyclotomic action. Number fields satisfy the required vanishing \(\operatorname{Hom}_{G_k}(\mathbf Z_\ell(1),T_\ell A)=0\) for every abelian variety \(A\) (Definition 26). This comparison concerns cusp inertia, not the handwritten Hodge or level filtrations.
